evidence: Receiving DO2 step change from 12.94 mg/L at 46.0 h to 8.50 mg/L at 46.2 h, continuing decline to 7.41 mg/L at 52.0 h
Source batches at 52 h: 10.88 (source-1), 10.81 (source-2), 11.47 (source-3) mg/L — receiving is 3+ mg/L below source envelope
Receiving P at 48 h = 3.025 g/L, matching source-1/2/3 at 48 h (3.057/3.017/2.979 g/L) — growth/product not yet compromised
DO2 remains above the 2 mg/L minimum constraint even at the 52 h minimum of 7.41 mg/L
No feed-related evidence of excess or limitation in available observations
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 abruptly fell at 46.2 h (12.9 → 8.2 mg/L) and has declined steadily to 7.4 mg/L by 52 h, while all three source batches at the same age still run ~10.5–11.5 mg/L. The product trajectory (P ≈ 3.03 g/L at 48 h, matching sources at ~3.0 g/L) shows production is on track, so the deviation is consistent with oxygen uptake demand outstripping transfer capacity in the receiving vessel, not a feed excess. increase_air raises the aeration factor within its bounded range (1.0 → 1.15), directly addressing the OTR shortfall without cutting feed and thus without sacrificing product mass, and keeps DO comfortably above the 2 mg/L minimum. Alternatives considered: KEEP risks continued DO decline and eventual oxygen-limited production; reduce_feed/combined/strong feed cuts reduce substrate and likely product mass without evidence of feed-related cause; stop yields zero counted production. No extra assay was requested: the online DO2 evidence is unambiguous and a 4 h assay delay would not change the oxygen-transfer diagnosis.
args.uncertainty: The exact aeration headroom of the receiving vessel is unknown; if blower/OTR capacity is already near its limit, a 15% increase may only partially restore DO. Hidden receiving parameters may also include a different oxygen demand kinetics than sources, so the DO recovery magnitude is uncertain. Feed state is unobserved, so a covert feed excess cannot be fully excluded — if DO fails to recover post-intervention, feed reduction would be the next bounded step.
